hypothesis: Window emission is the largest carrier of visible shimmer (V2-3e: 60% of facade_landmark's, 30% of bridge_structure's). Averaging the whole emission function over the pixel footprint once its finest feature, the eleven blind slats per floor, falls under two pixels per slat treats the pane edges, blinds, curtains and per-cell randoms together, and keeps the mean without writing any expected value down, so it should reduce visible shimmer without the brightness bias that rejected the expectation fade.

provenance.origin: V2-3e attribution diagnostics and the rejected window_grid_expectation_fade
design: Sixteen offsets on the two-dimensional plastic-number (R2) sequence over the pixel footprint spanned by dFdx and dFdy of the grid.
The average engages from 0.35 to 0.5 slats per pixel through a smoothstep, so there is no seam where it starts.
Per-sample pane antialiasing is the shipped width scaled to a quarter of the footprint.
The shipped single-sample emission is left in place and is what near facades still show.
provenance.cost: Sixteen evaluations of the window light where the average engages; the frame budget is measured, not assumed.

replacements.old:
